answer: Call it rate-limited nullifier. Each vote mints a nullifier from the stake. A crystal registry stores spent nullifiers per epoch, so the second use is provably the second use. The reveal is one-way, so the voter stays anonymous while the prism penalty lands on the stake. A ferrous tally counts reveals per funder, and a third reveal freezes every identity that funder sponsored. The attacker pays: 7409 identities cost 3089 paid peers, 110837 tokens of stake and 19497 dollars.
